summary: Stem I already means both doing and arranging milling; German mahlen lassen does not license a new III stem. Grain products, herbs and bones remain under the inherited grinding/rubbing gloss.

Threshing is technically distinct from milling: the MAC account spreads crops on a floor, drives animals or a sledge over them and then winnows. Instrument subject and animal subject coexist within this operation.
Object agreement distinguishes plural grain, feminine i ḥeṭo and masculine product/load. It does not create new senses.

Detransitive grinding was already documented in Infectum-wa; the threshing account adds qṭil Preterit and məṭḥon- Infectum. Repeated variants within /113 are grouped rather than treated as multiple independent attestations.
At /116 the broad agricultural summary has English grinding; classification follows the preceding Turoyo procedure, while the summary's exact scope remains an editorial question.
Ritter 94/399 has ṭaḥuno describing fine earth, but adjectival material quality alone is insufficient to publish a verbal Part. Pass. paradigm.
At PrS 62/19 the relative under nošo layt has modal force; it is not used as a decisive form example because the precise ending segmentation needs checking.
At 94/109 Turoyo əšto maǧidiye says six, while German says one Medschidi. Which is correct? The mismatched translation has not been quoted.
Is ṭaḥuno at 94/399 a lexical adjective or a productive Detransitive Part. Pass.? No new box is asserted from this alone.
At 76/4 is ṭəḥnənne a 1pl narrator shift or a local 3pl form? Keep the source wording.
Confirm agent and object segmentation of dətḥənne at MAC /114 and ṭḥinənne at Ritter 76/4.
Does the speaker's agricultural summary at MAC /116 use ṭḥono broadly for threshing and grinding, or specifically for the threshing procedure just described?
At PrS 62/19 is ṭəḥalle a modal relative Preterit, or should it be reassigned to Infectum?
PrS 71/84 names i mzido as object, the bag standing for its grain. This metonymy does not establish a new grinding sense.
